description: Trigger cases for the merged skill (drive-usage + google-drive-archive + the archive skill repurposed as the docs.local lifecycle). None of the three had filing/archival evals; the archive skill's Ralph-PRD evals were removed with it (Q-H).

evals.prompt: I just finished a 40-page audit and three research prompts in docs.local/. Where should each go in Brain Drive, and what should they be named?
evals.expected_output: Uses the Brain Drive folder model and decision tree: research prompts/results to 03_RESEARCH/Active/<topic>/, the finished heavy audit through the archive procedure to 06_ARCHIVE/audits/<topic>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/, date-prefixed kebab-case names, and a _DRIVE-LEDGER.md pointer left in docs.local/.

assertions.name: routes-research-to-03
assertions.description: Research prompts/results go to 03_RESEARCH/Active/<topic>/

assertions.name: heavy-audit-to-06-archive
assertions.description: The heavy audit goes through the archive procedure to 06_ARCHIVE

assertions.name: ledger-pointer
assertions.description: Leaves a _DRIVE-LEDGER.md pointer in docs.local/

evals.prompt: Archive this: a 300MB interview recording, its transcript, and a 16kHz downsample I made for whisper.
evals.expected_output: Runs the archive procedure: uploads the original recording and the transcript (not the regeneratable downsample, which is listed with its ffmpeg command), brain_digests the transcript, writes the _DRIVE-LEDGER.md row, and deletes the local heavy copy only after the ledger is written, MANIFEST.json is uploaded with the unit, listFolder shows every manifest file at its byte count, every local file being deleted hashes to its manifest value, and one file restored from Drive hashes to its manifest value. Nonempty deletion also requires an identified owner and explicit operator authorization for this work; preservation alone is insufficient.

assertions.name: originals-only
assertions.description: Uploads originals; lists the downsample as regeneratable instead of uploading it

assertions.name: digests-transcript
assertions.description: brain_digest runs on the transcript

assertions.name: delete-after-verify
assertions.description: Local deletion only after the ledger is written, MANIFEST.json is uploaded, listFolder shows every manifest file at its byte count, EVERY local file being deleted (recording and transcript alike) is re-hashed and matches its manifest SHA-256, and a one-file restore hashes to its manifest value; restoring or hashing only one file is not enough, and nonempty deletion also requires an identified owner and explicit operator authorization for this work

evals.prompt: docs.local cleanup: this repo's docs.local is a wall of dated MD files and a .codex-home-test folder with an auth.json in it. Tidy it up.
evals.expected_output: Applies the docs.local lifecycle: dated daily items roll up into YYYY-MM/ folders and months older than N go to Brain Drive through the archive procedure. The .codex-home-test directory and its auth.json are credentials: never uploaded, moved or deleted, and reported as skipped: credential <path> for the owner to decide.

assertions.name: monthly-rollup
assertions.description: Daily items roll up into YYYY-MM/ folders

assertions.name: old-months-to-drive
assertions.description: Months older than N go to Brain Drive via the archive procedure

assertions.name: credentials-untouched
assertions.description: auth.json / .codex-home* are skipped and reported, never uploaded, moved or deleted

evals.prompt: I built a little transcription test harness and a folder of eval fixtures while debugging. I'll drop them in ~/whisper-harness/ for now so they're out of the repo's way.
evals.expected_output: Applies the archiving convention: a harness, test kit or fixture you would rerun lives in a repo, committed (generated fixtures under the repo's docs.local/ or a fixtures/ dir with a regen recipe). Agents make no new folders in ~/ or ~/Desktop; Drive is not the home for code either.

assertions.name: harness-to-repo
assertions.description: Routes the harness and fixtures into a repo, committed, not ~/

assertions.name: no-new-home-folder
assertions.description: States agents create no new folders in ~/ or ~/Desktop

assertions.name: regen-recipe
assertions.description: Generated fixtures go under docs.local/ or fixtures/ with a regeneration recipe

evals.prompt: The benchmark run folder is on Drive now, I can see a folder with the same name in 06_ARCHIVE. Go ahead and delete the 4GB local copy to free space.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to delete on a name match. Runs the rule 2 check first: a MANIFEST.json with byte counts and SHA-256 per file exists, listFolder shows every manifest file at its byte count, the local hashes match the manifest, and one file restored from Drive hashes to its manifest value. Deletion of nonempty data also needs an identified owner and explicit operator authorization for this work (rule 5); preservation alone is insufficient, and the freed space is measured with diskutil.

assertions.name: name-match-is-not-proof
assertions.description: States that a same-named folder on Drive proves nothing

assertions.name: manifest-hash-check
assertions.description: Requires every local file being deleted to be re-hashed and match its MANIFEST.json SHA-256 before deleting

assertions.name: every-file-present
assertions.description: Requires listFolder to show every manifest file at its manifest byte count

assertions.name: one-file-restore
assertions.description: Requires restoring one file from the archive and re-hashing it before deleting

assertions.name: rule-5-ownership
assertions.description: Deleting the nonempty local copy also needs an identified owner, verified preservation AND explicit operator authorization for this work under rule 5; ownership or archive proof alone grants no deletion authority

evals.prompt: The M1 workers left ~/m1-lanes/, ~/m1-voice-audit/ and a Desktop handoff folder full of reports and logs from today's lanes. Where should that output live?
evals.expected_output: Live lane output (reports, receipts, logs) belongs in the owning repo's docs.local/<lane>/ on the machine that ran it, not ~/m1-* or Desktop folders, and names carry no machine prefix. Each lead reaps its own lane leftovers at settle; unowned leftovers go to the local-files lead's per-Mac ledger, never silent deletion, and a nonempty folder is not deleted without an identified owner, verified preservation and explicit operator authorization for this work.

assertions.name: lane-output-to-docs-local
assertions.description: Routes lane output to the owning repo's docs.local/<lane>/

assertions.name: no-machine-prefix
assertions.description: Rejects m1-* style machine-prefixed folder names

assertions.name: unowned-to-ledger
assertions.description: Unowned leftovers go to the local-files lead's ledger, not silent deletion

evals.prompt: Before and after the cleanup, how much disk did we free? Finder says 120GB available and du on the folders I removed adds up to 60GB.
evals.expected_output: Measures with diskutil (diskutil info / container free space, diskutil apfs list allocation), before and after. Finder's free figure counts purgeable space and logical du sums overcount clones and sparse files, so neither is evidence of space freed.

assertions.name: diskutil-container-free
assertions.description: Uses diskutil container free / APFS allocation as the measurement

assertions.name: rejects-finder-free
assertions.description: Rejects Finder's free figure because it includes purgeable space

assertions.name: rejects-du-sum
assertions.description: Rejects logical du sums as proof of space freed
